name: Threat
summary: Threat-intelligence entities (malware, campaigns, operations, vulnerabilities, threat actors, indicators, attack patterns, tools, detection signatures) and their relationships, aligned with STIX 2.1.
description:
Node types for threat-intelligence work: the software used in an attack (malware, tools), who is behind it (threat actors), the activity it belongs to (campaigns and the operations inside them), the weakness and technique it uses (vulnerabilities, ATT&CK attack patterns), and how it is detected (indicators, detection signatures, and a scanner's verdict on a sample). The types follow STIX 2.1 concepts.

The pack is data only: it defines ten node types in the `threat` category and runs no code. It declares no edge types; "uses", "attributed to" and every other relationship is recorded as an edge in the project.

## Types

| Type | Label | What it represents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threat.malware` | `name` | A malware family or sample, with hashes and a sighting timeline |
| `threat.file_hash` | `sha256` | A scanner's verdict on one sample, identified by its SHA-256 |
| `threat.campaign` | `campaign_name` | A coordinated set of malicious activities over a period of time |
| `threat.operation` | `operation_name` | One bounded operation within a campaign: a specific wave, intrusion or offensive action |
| `threat.threat_actor` | `actor_name` | An individual, group or organisation believed to operate with malicious intent |
| `threat.vulnerability` | `cve_id` | A CVE-tracked software vulnerability with severity and affected product |
| `threat.indicator` | `value` | An indicator of compromise: an abstract, confidence-scored observable |
| `threat.attack_pattern` | `name` | An adversary technique, mapped where possible to MITRE ATT&CK |
| `threat.tool` | `name` | Legitimate or offensive software an actor uses to carry out activity |
| `threat.signature` | `name` | A detection rule (YARA, Sigma, Snort, ...) |

Each type is identified by its label field alone: two nodes with the same label are one entity.

## Notable properties and relationships

- **Malware.** `malware_type` is required as well as `name`: one of `trojan`, `ransomware`, `worm`, `loader`, `backdoor`, `rat`, `stealer`, `rootkit`, `botnet`, `downloader`, `wiper`, `spyware`, `adware`, `other`, `unknown`. Also `platform` (`windows`, `linux`, `macos`, `android`, `ios`, `multi`), `is_family` (a family rather than a single sample), `hash_md5`, `hash_sha1`, `hash_sha256`, `aliases` (one entry per name), `first_seen` and `last_seen`.
- **File hash.** The reputation counts belong to a named product (VirusTotal and the like), not to the file: `malicious_count`, `suspicious_count`, `undetected_count` and `times_submitted`, with `sha1`, `md5`, `size`, `type_description` (such as "Win32 EXE"), scanner `tags` and `first_seen`. It is not the same thing as `endpoint.file` in the Endpoint pack, which is a file seen at a place on a host; the two are linked with an edge rather than merged. Two verdicts on the same hash are one node.
- **Campaign and operation.** One campaign can contain several operations. A campaign has `objective`, `status` (`active`, `dormant`, `concluded`), `first_seen`, `start_date`, `end_date` and a free-text `attribution` to a suspected actor. An operation has its own `objective`, `status` (`planned`, `active`, `dormant`, `concluded`, `failed`) and dates. Both have a `description`.
- **Threat actor.** `actor_type` (`nation-state`, `cybercriminal`, `hacktivist`, `insider`, `terrorist`, `unknown`), `motivation` (`espionage`, `financial`, `ideological`, `destructive`, `notoriety`, `unknown`), `sophistication` (`minimal`, `intermediate`, `advanced`, `strategic`), suspected `country`, `known_aliases` and `first_seen`.
- **Vulnerability.** `cve_id` must have the form `CVE-YYYY-NNNN` (four or more digits at the end). Also `cvss_score` (0 to 10), `severity` (`none` to `critical`), `cvss_vector`, `cwe_id` (`CWE-<n>`), `exploited_in_wild`, `affected_product`, `description` and `published_date`.
- **Indicator.** Meant to be linked to the concrete typed node it identifies, such as an `infrastructure.ip_address` or an `endpoint.file`. `indicator_type` is one of `ipv4`, `ipv6`, `domain`, `url`, `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `email`, `filename`, `registry_key`, `mutex`; also `confidence` (`low`, `medium`, `high`), `valid_from` and `description`.
- **Attack pattern.** `technique_id` in ATT&CK form (`T1234` or `T1234.001`) and `tactic`, one of the 14 ATT&CK tactics from `reconnaissance` to `impact`.
- **Tool.** `tool_type` (`c2`, `rat`, `loader`, `stealer`, `exploitation`, `post-exploitation`, `recon`, `utility`), `aliases` and `description`.
- **Detection signature.** `signature_type` (`yara`, `sigma`, `snort`, `suricata`, `clamav`), the `rule` body and a `description` of what it detects.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/typepack-basic (file `typepacks/threat.json`). Licence: Apache-2.0.

types.name: malware
types.description: A malware family or sample with hashes and a sighting timeline.

is_family.description: True if this represents a family rather than a single sample.

aliases.description: Other names the malware is tracked under — one entry per name.

types.name: file_hash
types.description: A scanner’s verdict on one sample, identified by its SHA-256 — the reputation counts here belong to a named product (VirusTotal and the like), not to the file itself. NOT the same thing as endpoint.file, which is a file seen at a place on a host: link the two with an edge rather than merging them. Two verdicts on the same hash are the same node.

type_description.description: Vendor type description, e.g. "Win32 EXE" or "PDF document".

malicious_count.description: Number of engines that flagged the file malicious.

suspicious_count.description: Number of engines that flagged the file suspicious.

undetected_count.description: Number of engines that did not detect the file.

times_submitted.description: Number of times the file has been submitted to the scanner.

types.name: campaign
types.description: A coordinated set of malicious activities over a period of time.

objective.description: Goal of the campaign (e.g. espionage, financial theft).

types.name: operation
types.description: A single, bounded operation within a campaign: a specific wave, intrusion, or offensive action with its own timeline and objectives. Think of it as a subset of a campaign — one campaign can contain multiple operations.

types.name: threat_actor
types.description: An individual, group, or organization believed to operate with malicious intent.

types.name: vulnerability
types.description: A CVE-tracked software vulnerability with severity and affected product.

exploited_in_wild.description: Known to be exploited in the wild.

types.name: indicator
types.description: An indicator of compromise (IOC): an abstract, confidence-scored observable. Link it to the concrete typed node it identifies (e.g. infrastructure.ip_address, endpoint.file) with the refers_to edge.

indicator_type.description: What kind of artifact the value is.

valid_from.description: Time from which the indicator is considered valid.

types.name: attack_pattern
types.description: An adversary technique, mapped where possible to MITRE ATT&CK.

types.name: tool
types.description: Legitimate or offensive software used by an actor to carry out activity.

aliases.description: Other names for the tool — one entry per name.

types.name: signature
types.description: A detection rule (YARA, Sigma, Snort, ...) used to identify threats.
